title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 1. Purpose
This Manual sets out MC’s operating practices, meeting formats, attendance rules, book/data procedures, and fee administration. It may be updated more easily than the Governance Protocol.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 2. Meeting Types
MC conducts three categories of meetings:

Tour Critique Meetings
Executive Development Meetings
Special Meetings

MC intends to meet three times each year within planning windows established by the membership.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 3. Annual Schedule
The Secretary shall maintain the rolling three-year schedule.
MC should ordinarily meet within these windows unless otherwise approved:

January 15 to February 15
May 15 to June 15
September 15 to October 15

Meeting type mix may be set by the members from time to time. Historical patterns may guide scheduling but do not bind future years.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 4. Critique Meeting Format
A Critique Meeting ordinarily includes:

travel periods,
company specific presentations,
host facility tours,
structured critique session,
philosophy or leadership discussion,
Executive Session,
MC book review.
Presentations of interest by moderator or external visitors

The host company shall distribute a pre-read packet sufficiently in advance. The critique process is intended to be candid, practical, and respectful. The host should identify specific questions or decision areas on which feedback is requested.
Each company shall prepare for a Critique Meeting by:

Submitting a What’s New document summarizing activities and performance since prior meeting.
Reviewing other member company What’s New documents and submitting observations or questions of interest.
Submitting any documentation needed for the company specific presentations.

These items shall typically be completed within the prior two weeks of each meeting.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 5. Host Company Responsibilities
The Host should:

select and coordinate plant/store visits,
plan logistics,
identify the desired focus areas,
prepare host materials,
designate any host-only invitees,
coordinate meal and transportation arrangements as needed,
submit shared expenses for allocation.

The host packet may include:

company overview,
executive team overview,
local market and competitive context,
location-level summaries,
financial snapshots,
strategic questions,
feedback forms,
operating concerns to explore.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 6. What’s New Reports
Each member company shall prepare a concise What’s New report in advance of each regular meeting. The report should focus on major developments, experiments, challenges, wins, risks, and discussion items of value to the group.
MC has adopted a standard format and created a template for distribution prior to each meeting.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
section: Section 7. Book Review and Data Sharing
text:
Section 7. Book Review and Data Sharing
“The Book” is the recurring financial and operating performance package compiled for MC.
Each member company shall submit required data no later than the 15th of the following month unless modified by the Book Manager and Executive Committee.
The Book may include company-identified information, but access shall be restricted to approved recipients under this Manual and the Charter.
MC acknowledges that company-specific exchange of sensitive competitor information requires care. The Book Manager, moderator, and Executive Committee should work together to present data in ways that support learning while reducing legal risk, including through lagging, normalization, summarization, or aggregation where feasible. Current FTC/DOJ guidance stresses caution around competitor exchanges involving price, cost, discounts, wages, and strategic plans.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 8. Book Manager
The Book Manager shall:

collect monthly submissions,
maintain required reporting formats,
prepare the Book,
distribute it securely,
maintain recipient records,
coordinate with meeting planners on Book review topics.

The Book Manager is elected or appointed as determined by MC.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 9. Data Access and Security
Access to the Book and related MC materials is limited to:

Owners,
approved Principals,
approved eligible executives,
the moderator,
Book Manager or designated data administrator,
others specifically approved by the Executive Committee.

Each member company is responsible for internal handling of MC materials.
MC materials shall not be forwarded beyond approved recipients without permission.
When a member resigns or is terminated, access to current Book distribution shall end promptly, and MC shall follow its retention/deletion procedures.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 10. Attendance and Eligible Attendees
The standard expectation is that attendees are owner-operators and senior executives.
Unless the host and Executive Committee approve otherwise, attendance is limited to three persons per member company.
Attendance categories:

Voting Representative(s): owner/operator or designated equivalent.
Approved Principals: individuals approved for regular attendance.
Approved Senior Executives: non-principal leaders whose attendance has been approved in advance.
Host-Only Employees: employees of the host company invited only to the critique-related portions designated by the host.

Non-principal attendees from member companies should ordinarily be limited to one or two senior executives whose participation is directly relevant to the agenda.
Any attendee not already approved for routine attendance must be approved in advance by both the Executive Committee and the Host.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 11. Attendance Expectations
Each member company is expected to ensure regular participation by an owner/operator.
If the owner/operator is absent from two meetings in a calendar year or two consecutive regular meetings, the Executive Committee shall review the situation and recommend whether any action is warranted, including warning, probation, or membership vote.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 12. Executive Development Meetings
An Executive Development Meeting may use the same broad time blocks as a Critique Meeting but focuses primarily on group-wide development topics.
The moderator, Executive Committee, and host if applicable shall design the agenda.
Family/spouse attendance is not presumed. Any family or social attendance components must be expressly approved for that event and separated from confidential business sessions.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 13. Special Meetings
Any member company may request a Special Meeting to address urgent or significant issues.
Attendance, structure, scope, confidentiality terms, and cost allocation shall be determined for that meeting by the Executive Committee in consultation with the requesting member.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 14. Executive Session Procedures
Executive Session is normally scheduled near the close of each regular meeting.
The moderator may remain to facilitate and record approved notes unless excused by the Executive Committee.
The Executive Committee may excuse any person, including the moderator, from all or part of the Executive Session.
Only approved attendees may remain.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 15. Notes, Materials, and Follow-Up
The Secretary or moderator, as assigned, shall circulate only the level of notes approved by MC.
MC may distinguish among:

governance minutes,
meeting summaries,
action items,
host critique feedback,
confidential discussion notes not circulated broadly.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 16. Fees and Expense Allocation
Each member company shall pay:

its own travel and lodging,
recurring MC fees as adopted by MC,
allocated meeting costs,
any special charges approved in advance.

Unless MC adopts a different budget structure:

common meeting costs are divided equally among member companies,
meal costs may be prorated by attendance,
prospect-visit costs may be spread as approved by MC,
moderator and Book fees are administered according to approved schedules.

Current fees should live in a separate annual schedule, not in this Manual.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
section: Section 17. Prospect Visits and Trial Attendance
text:
Section 17. Prospect Visits and Trial Attendance
Prospects may attend only under terms set by the Executive Committee.
Before receiving sensitive information, a prospect must sign MC’s confidentiality and compliance documents.
The Executive Committee may limit what portions of a meeting a prospect may attend and what materials the prospect may receive.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 18. Compliance Practices
At the start of each Book session and Executive Session, the moderator or Chair should remind participants:

each company makes independent business decisions,
no discussion should seek coordination on prices, discounts, wages, customers, territories, or strategic conduct,
sensitive topics may be redirected or stopped.

title: Proposed Operating Manual
text:
Section 19. Amendments to Manual
This Manual may be amended by majority vote or such higher threshold as MC chooses, provided the amendment does not conflict with the Governance Charter.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 1. Name and Purpose
Management Concepts (“MC”) is a voluntary association of independently owned and operated textile maintenance businesses. MC exists to improve the quality of leadership, decision-making, operations, and long-term performance of its member companies through structured peer learning, disciplined comparison, candid discussion, and mutual support. MC is not a partnership, joint venture, trade association with lobbying functions, or entity with authority over any member company’s independent business decisions.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 2. Guiding Principles
Members commit to:

Candor in sharing relevant experience and performance information.
Respectful and constructive critique.
Strict confidentiality.
Independent decision-making by each company.
Active participation and reciprocity.
Compliance with applicable law, including competition law.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 3. Membership
MC may have no more than thirteen member companies at any time. The target operating size for MC is twelve member companies.
A member company must be independently owned or controlled and operate in the textile maintenance industry.
Each member company shall identify:

at least one Owner-Operator or equivalent senior owner,
any approved Principals, and
any approved additional executives eligible to attend certain meetings under the Operating Manual.

Membership is held by the company, not by any individual person.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 4. Admission of New Members
A prospective member may be nominated by a current member. Before invitation to join:

the Executive Committee shall conduct preliminary screening for fit and conflicts,
two members designated by the Executive Committee shall conduct a visit or equivalent diligence review,
the prospect shall receive and sign MC’s confidentiality and compliance acknowledgments before receiving sensitive materials,
the prospect may be invited to attend a meeting under terms set by the Executive Committee, and
admission requires unanimous approval of all member companies entitled to vote.

The Executive Committee may adopt additional admission criteria in the Operating Manual, including size, geography, overlap, and conflict review.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 5. Termination, Resignation, and Suspension
A member may resign at any time by written notice to the Chair and Secretary.
Membership may be suspended or terminated for cause, including:

material breach of confidentiality,
conduct materially inconsistent with MC’s purpose,
repeated nonparticipation,
failure to meet fee obligations,
legal or ethical conduct that materially undermines group trust.

Except in extraordinary circumstances, the process shall include:

Written notice,
Executive Committee review,
Opportunity for the member to respond,
Recommendation by the Executive Committee, and
Vote by the member companies entitled to vote.

Termination requires unanimous approval of all other member companies entitled to vote.
The Executive Committee may impose interim restrictions, including suspension of access to data, documents, or attendance privileges, pending final action.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 6. Governance Structure
MC shall be governed by an Executive Committee including:

a Chair,
a Vice Chair,
a Secretary,

The Executive Committee is responsible for stewardship of MC, interpretation of this Charter, supervision of governance administration, and matters requiring judgment between meetings.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 7. Officers and Terms
The officer roles include:
Chair: 
external representative of MC, leader of governance matters, partner to the moderator.
Vice Chair: 
supports the Chair; oversees treasury, membership pipeline, and related administrative matters.
Secretary: 
maintains governance records, approved minutes of Executive Session, officer records, amendments, and official notices.

Terms shall be two years unless otherwise set by vote of the members.
MC may retain additional administrative roles under the Operating Manual, including Moderator, Book Manager and Email/Data Manager. These are operating roles, not governance officers unless separately designated.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 8. Elections and Succession
Officers shall be elected at the Executive Session or at another duly designated meeting. Election procedures shall be specified in the Operating Manual.
Officers shall be elected by majority vote of member companies present and entitled to vote. MC may consider rotation and succession customs but shall not be required to do so.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 9. Meetings of the Membership
MC shall hold regular meetings as described in the Operating Manual. Governance matters requiring formal action may be taken:

during Executive Session at a meeting,
by remote meeting, or
by written/electronic vote between meetings.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 10. Voting
Each member company has one vote.
Unless otherwise stated, action requires a simple majority of member companies present and entitled to vote.
The following require unanimous approval of all member companies entitled to vote, excluding the affected member where applicable:

admission of a new member,
termination of membership,
retention of a moderator under a long-form engagement,
addition of a company-specific Principal list category if treated as a governance matter (see Article 3).

Amendments to this Charter require:

quorum of at least ten member companies, and
approval by at least 75% of all member companies then in membership, rounded up.

Proxy voting may be allowed only if authorized in writing before the vote and only for matters not prohibited by the Operating Manual.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 11. Quorum
For ordinary governance business during a meeting, quorum is a majority of member companies present.
For Charter amendments, quorum is ten member companies.
For actions requiring unanimity, all member companies entitled to vote must have notice and opportunity to participate, whether in person, remotely, or by permitted written ballot.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 12. Moderator
MC may retain a moderator/facilitator under a written agreement approved by the member companies.
The moderator’s role is to facilitate meetings, assist with planning, support constructive dialogue, and perform other duties assigned by agreement.
The moderator is not a voting member and does not govern MC.
The moderator may attend Executive Session to facilitate discussion and record approved notes unless excused. The Executive Committee may, by majority decision, excuse the moderator or any attendee from all or part of Executive Session when needed for member privacy, conflict management, personnel-sensitive matters, legal sensitivity, compensation discussions, or other good cause.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 13. Executive Session
Executive Session is the private governance session of MC.
Attendance is limited to:

approved voting representatives of member companies,
the moderator unless excused under Article 12,
any other person specifically approved by the Executive Committee for a defined purpose.

Topics may include:

governance,
membership matters,
schedule and planning,
moderator review,
compliance matters,
issues requiring candid member-only discussion.

The Secretary shall maintain governance notes or minutes in the level of detail approved by MC.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 14. Confidentiality
All nonpublic information shared through MC, whether oral, written, visual, digital, or observational, is confidential and may not be disclosed outside MC except with the express consent of the originating member company or as required by law.
This duty applies to:

current members,
prospective members,
former members,
current and former moderators,
guests,
approved employees and attendees.

Each member company is responsible for ensuring its attendees comply.
The Executive Committee shall maintain a confidentiality acknowledgment form for all eligible attendees.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 15. Competition Law Compliance
Because MC consists of competing businesses, each member remains solely responsible for its own business decisions, including prices, discounts, wages, staffing, service offerings, territories, vendors, customers, marketing, and strategic plans.
MC shall not be used to propose, coordinate, signal, recommend, or facilitate agreement on any competitively sensitive matter. Prohibited discussion topics include, except as cleared by counsel in a compliant format:

current or future prices, fees, surcharges, discounts, or markups,
wage rates, compensation structures, benefits, or hiring restrictions,
allocation of territories, customers, or accounts,
coordinated refusals to deal,
future expansion, contraction, capacity, or output plans,
nonpublic customer-specific or vendor-specific negotiation strategy.

The moderator and Chair shall have authority to stop or redirect discussions that create competition-law risk. MC may require use of lagged, normalized, aggregated, or manager-administered reporting methods where appropriate.
This section reflects current FTC/DOJ caution about competitor information exchanges and independent pricing and wage decisions.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 16. Records
The Secretary shall maintain:

this Charter and amendment history,
official officer records,
formal votes,
approved Executive Session notes,
member acknowledgments required by MC.

Operating records may be maintained under the Operating Manual.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 17. Indemnity / Liability Disclaimer
MC is a voluntary peer group. It does not provide legal, accounting, tax, investment, employment, or other professional advice. Members remain responsible for their own decisions and compliance obligations.

title: Proposed Charter
text:
Article 18. Amendments
This Charter may be amended only in accordance with Article 10.

title: Governance
text:
Editing from existing to proposed
This section includes:

the Existing Protocol approved on February 20, 2007.
Proposed drafts of a Charter and Operating Manual to replace the existing protocol.
The current slate of officers.

Per section 1.2 of the existing Protocol

Any amendments made to the Protocol must be approved by at least a 75% affirmative vote (rounding up) and the vote must have quorum. For the purposes of changing Protocol, quorum is 10 Members and 8 members must vote affirmatively to the proposed Protocol changes. There is only 1 vote per Member company.

Example of a change regarding voting is more clarity in the Proposed Charter, defining Article 10: Voting and Article 11: Quorum.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
The original 2007 Protocol served Management Concepts well for many years. It captured the group’s core values and operating assumptions, including confidentiality, candid peer review, regular meetings, member voting, shared financial reporting through “The Book,” and a rotating leadership structure. It also combined several different kinds of material in one document: governance rules, meeting procedures, attendance rules, fee arrangements, current officer names, and the moderator contract. The proposed Charter and Operating Manual reorganize that material into a structure that is easier to read, easier to maintain, and better aligned with how the group operates today.

title: Protocol_Revision_Steps
text: The original 2007 Protocol served Management Concepts well for many years. It captured the group’s core values and operating assumptions, including confidentiality, candid peer review, regular meetings, member voting, shared financial reporting through “The Book,” and a rotating leadership structure. It also combined several different kinds of material in one document: governance rules, meeting procedures, attendance rules, fee arrangements, current officer names, and the moderator contract. The proposed Charter and Operating Manual reorganize that material into a structure that is easier to read, easier to maintain, and better aligned with how the group operates today.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
Why this change was made


View section

The change was made to separate long-term governance rules from day-to-day operating practices. The 2007 Protocol placed both in one document, along with time-sensitive items such as current officer names, cost schedules, and the moderator contract. The proposed Charter now holds the core governance framework, while the Operating Manual holds the practical procedures for meetings, attendance, “The Book,” and administration. This should make the documents easier to use and easier to update over time.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
What was preserved


View section

The rewrite was intended to preserve the core identity of Management Concepts rather than replace it. The following central ideas from the 2007 Protocol were carried forward:

MC remains a confidential peer group of independently owned companies whose purpose is to share knowledge for the benefit of members.
The Executive Committee remains the core governance structure, consisting of Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary.
Confidentiality remains one of the group’s defining principles.
Membership remains selective and subject to structured review and unanimous approval.
Meetings, critiques, and “The Book” remain central to how MC operates.

In short, the values and operating logic of the 2007 Protocol were preserved, even when the wording or location changed.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
What was reorganized


View section

One of the main goals of the rewrite was to move material into the document where it most naturally belongs.
The Charter now focuses on:

purpose and guiding principles
membership
admission and termination
officer roles
voting and quorum
the moderator’s governance role
executive session
confidentiality
records and amendments

The Operating Manual now focuses on:

meeting types and annual schedule
critique meeting format
host responsibilities
What’s New reports
Book preparation and distribution
data access and security
attendance categories
executive session procedures
fees and expense allocation
prospect attendance procedures

This reorganization was meant to make the documents easier to navigate, not to change the culture of the group.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
What was clarified or modernized


View section

Several parts of the 2007 Protocol were kept in substance but rewritten for clarity and current use.

Voting and quorum: the proposed Charter organizes voting rules more clearly so it is easier to tell what threshold applies to which decision.
Moderator role: the moderator remains a non-voting facilitator, but the Executive Committee is now explicitly allowed to excuse the moderator or any attendee from all or part of Executive Session when appropriate.
Attendance categories: the Operating Manual defines voting representatives, approved principals, approved senior executives, and host-only employees more clearly than the old Protocol.
Attendance expectations: the old automatic trigger for a membership vote after missed meetings was softened into an Executive Committee review process that can recommend warning, probation, or further action.
Data handling: the Operating Manual adds more explicit language on approved access, internal handling, and removal of access when a member leaves.

These changes were intended to improve clarity and administration while keeping the same basic expectations.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
What was added


View section

A few items were added because they are more important or more visible now than they were in 2007.

Competition-law compliance: the Charter now includes a section stating that each member company remains responsible for its own independent business decisions, and the Operating Manual adds a short reminder for Book sessions and Executive Session.
Records and acknowledgments: the Charter more clearly identifies records maintained by the Secretary and the use of confidentiality acknowledgments for eligible attendees.
Data access and security: the Operating Manual adds a dedicated section on who may access “The Book” and how MC materials should be handled.

These additions were meant to support the same trust-based model that has always existed, while making responsibilities clearer in writing.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
section: What was removed from the governing document
text:
What was removed from the governing document


View section

Some material from the 2007 Protocol was not carried forward into the core governance documents because it was temporary, administrative, or historical rather than foundational.

Current officer names: these belong in a current officers page or annual record, not in the permanent Charter.
Current fee schedules: these are time-sensitive and better maintained separately from the governing documents.
The moderator contract: this is still important, but it is better handled as a separate agreement rather than as an exhibit inside the core governance document.
Some historical detail: certain older administrative specifics were shortened, relocated to the Operating Manual, or removed where they no longer functioned well as permanent rules.

These items were not removed because they were unimportant. They were removed because they fit better in separate current records or agreements.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
section: What this rewrite is trying to accomplish
text:
What this rewrite is trying to accomplish


View section

The rewrite is trying to do four things:

preserve the values and operating logic of the 2007 Protocol,
make the governance framework easier to understand,
make operating procedures easier to update, and
remove historical and administrative clutter from the core governing document.

In that sense, the proposed Charter and Operating Manual are not meant to replace the identity of Management Concepts. They are meant to organize it more clearly for current and future use.

title: Protocol Redraft Process
text:
Questions for member review


View section

As members review the proposed Charter and Operating Manual, the most useful questions may be:

Does the split between governance and operations make sense?
Does the Charter preserve the important principles of MC?
Does the Operating Manual reflect how MC actually functions today?
Are there any provisions from the 2007 Protocol that were unintentionally lost?
Are any of the new clarifications too restrictive, too vague, or not reflective of current practice?
